title: Constructibility and recorded operations of the completed sheaf kernel
statement: Fix a prime \(\ell\), a finite extension \(E/\mathbf Q_\ell\), and its valuation ring \(\mathcal O_E\). Let \(k\) be any field in which \(\ell\) is invertible. Let \(X\) be a separated finite-type \(k\)-scheme, \(i:Z\hookrightarrow X\) a closed immersion, and \(j:U\hookrightarrow X\) its complementary open immersion over \(k\). With the actual completed-coefficient module unit \(\eta\) and kernel of [def-sf-recollement-presentation-data], let \(A\) be their exact derived presentation from [lem-sf-exact-localization-triangle]. Both functors of \(A\) preserve the integral constructible property [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Their literal restrictions [lem-sf-recollement-full-subcategory-restriction] are linear over the canonical \(\mathcal O_E\)-action. For every integral constructible \(K\) on \(X\), integral \(j^*K\) is constructible and the restricted open vertex is isomorphic to its recorded compact-support value; the underlying closed vertex is isomorphic to an object of the recorded integral direct-image tower for integral \(i^*K\) [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. This asserts no distinguished triangle or Hom vanishing.

source.place: Integral sheaf localization and coefficient passage, steps 3–10

proof.text: The structure map to k sends the unit l to a unit in each residue field of X, U, and Z. The recorded integral pullback preservation theorem therefore supplies constructibility of integral j*K and i*K.
The open-kernel compact-support comparison identifies the open vertex with the underlying recorded compact-support value. Transport its constructibility across that isomorphism.

The actual termwise kernel sequence gives a distinguished ambient localization triangle. Since the intrinsic constructible subcategory is triangulated and contains the open vertex and K, it contains the closed vertex. No separate finite closed-image constructibility theorem is required.

Naturality of the monic kernel counit forces the module open functor to be O_E-linear, by cancellation; naturality of the epic closed unit does the same for the closed functor. Descend linearity through the derived localization, identifying its scalar action with the canonical constant-section action. The literal full-subcategory restrictions inherit linearity.

Lift the open comparison to the full constructible subcategory. Apply the closed-kernel Roos comparison to K and i*K, whose completeness was already supplied by their constructibility. These give the two vertices required by the original unchanged statement.

theorem sfIntegralKernel_operation_realization
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : IsUnit (l : k))
    {Z U X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [U.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j]
    [j.IsOver (Spec (.of k))]
    (hij : Set.range j.base = (Set.range i.base)ᶜ) :
    letI := sfRecollementNoetherian k X
    let S := sfIntegralConstructible l E X
    let A := sfIntegralKernelAmbient l E i
    ∃ (ho : ∀ K : S.FullSubcategory, S (A.openTerm.obj K.obj))
      (hc : ∀ K : S.FullSubcategory, S (A.closedTerm.obj K.obj)),
      SfIntegralRecollementVertices l E k hk i j (sfRecollementRestriction S A ho hc) ∧
      (sfRecollementRestriction S A ho hc).openTerm.Linear
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E) ∧
      (sfRecollementRestriction S A ho hc).closedTerm.Linear
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)
